answer: One body, one account: iris-code match against a national biometric registry with liveness challenge means an iris code the registry matched live while the subject answered a randomised challenge. A farm would need a hundred living faces, each passing a fresh challenge the same morning, and every failed juniper attempt locks the account for a day. The kernel is the registry that remembers each iris it has seen, so a reused eye is caught at once. The shale is the cost of the scanner, the enrolment visit, and the queue - paid a hundred times, never once.
